fixes.explanation: Yes, friend, covenant. God says, “I will establish My covenant between Me and you…” A covenant is a binding promise, and this one comes straight from God Almighty. He adds, “…and I will multiply you exceedingly.” That is a LOT of multiplying. I bet Abram needed a minute, and he gets one. He falls facedown right there (Genesis 17:3).

That's the one, friend. God says Sarah will bear Isaac “…at this time next year.” Not someday. NEXT YEAR. That's a date you can put on the calendar. Right before this, Abraham laughs and asks, “Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old?” (Genesis 17:17). God answers with a timeline, and it's a short one.

problems.problem: It uses a reaction phrase. The code shows reactions; the explanation never does.
The joke links Abram’s age to trouble with his knees, making age the target of the humor. Also, multiplying knees is an unclear comparison to multiplying descendants.
Abraham is ninety-nine in this passage, not a hundred. The explanation also supplies a reason for his laughter that the text does not state.
